Direct curl gets a 403 (bot-challenged); fetched successfully via a browser-rendering fetch instead

notes: RapidPro/TextIt's REST API v2 documents 26 resources, but @openfn/language-rapidpro has no generic get/post/request builder: reading the adaptor's compiled source shows its four public functions (addContact, upsertContact, startFlow, sendBroadcast) each POST to exactly one fixed resource (contacts.json, flow_starts.json, broadcasts.json) built from a configurable host + apiVersion, and nothing else is reachable through it. coverage:full here means every documented method/field/filter of the four resources this adaptor can reach or reference (contacts, flow_starts, broadcasts, and flows, which flow_starts references by UUID but never itself calls) -- not the other ~22 REST v2 resources, which are out of scope. Previously this was a genuinely mislabelled spec: info.title was literally '(mock subset)' and the description said so too, modelling roughly a third of even these four resources' documented fields (no DELETE on contacts, no filters beyond the bare minimum, no query params on flow_starts/broadcasts/flows, thin Contact/FlowStart/Broadcast/Flow schemas). Rewritten field-for-field from the live per-resource docs pages (each resource has its own reference page under /api/v2/<resource>, consistently documenting GET/POST/DELETE, every field, and an example). upsertContact's own logic (POST without urns, and a second POST with ?urn=<urn> when the first response's urns[0] looks like an array) is an adaptor-side workaround, not a distinct endpoint; the underlying resource is the same POST /api/v2/contacts.json?urn=... modelled here. Host and API version are configurable per credential (app.rapidpro.io used as the default server), matching self-hosted RapidPro instances.
